title: Twenty-Seven Points
statement: Let $S$ be the set of the $27$ points $(x, y, z)$ in space whose coordinates $x$, $y$ and $z$ each belong to $\{0, 1, 2\}$. For each of the $\binom{27}{3}$ sets of three distinct points of $S$, square the area of the triangle with those three points as vertices, where three collinear points count as a triangle of area $0$. Let $T$ be the sum of all these squared areas. Find the remainder when $T$ is divided by $1000$.
hints: Look at the shadows of a triangle on the three coordinate planes. How is the area of the triangle related to the areas of its three shadows?

The squared area of a triangle in space is the sum of the squared areas of its projections onto the planes $x = 0$, $y = 0$ and $z = 0$, because these areas are half the components of a cross product. So by symmetry you need only the squared areas of the plane triangles whose vertices are projections of points of $S$. Write twice a signed area as $d(P_1, P_2) + d(P_2, P_3) + d(P_3, P_1)$ with $d(P, Q) = x_Py_Q - x_Qy_P$, and sum its square over ordered triples of points.

Shift the coordinates to $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ first. Then every cross term such as $d(P_1, P_2)\,d(P_2, P_3)$ sums to $0$ over the ordered triples, and each square term sums to $27\sum_{P, Q} d(P, Q)^2 = 27 \cdot 2\bigl(\sum x^2 \sum y^2 - (\sum xy)^2\bigr)$.
solution:
For points $P$, $Q$, $R$ in space, the vector $(Q - P) \times (R - P)$ has length twice the area of triangle $PQR$, and its three components are, up to sign, twice the areas of the projections of the triangle onto the planes $x = 0$, $y = 0$ and $z = 0$. So the squared area is the sum of the squared areas of the three projections, and by symmetry $T = 3T_z$, where $T_z$ is the sum of the squared areas of the projections onto the plane $z = 0$.

Shifting every coordinate down by $1$ changes no area, so take the coordinates in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. For points of the plane write $d(P, Q) = x_Py_Q - x_Qy_P$; twice the signed area of $P_1P_2P_3$ is $d(P_1, P_2) + d(P_2, P_3) + d(P_3, P_1)$. Sum its square over all $27^3$ ordered triples $(P_1, P_2, P_3)$ of points of $S$, each projected onto $z = 0$. Triples with a repeated point contribute $0$, and each $3$-element set appears $6$ times. Every cross term, such as $d(P_1, P_2)\,d(P_2, P_3)$, is linear in the coordinates of one of the points, here $P_1$, and $\sum x = \sum y = 0$ over $S$, so the cross terms add up to $0$. Each of the three square terms gives

$$27\sum_{P, Q \in S} d(P, Q)^2 = 27 \cdot 2\Bigl(\sum x^2 \sum y^2 - \bigl(\sum xy\bigr)^2\Bigr) = 27 \cdot 2 \cdot (18 \cdot 18 - 0) = 17496,$$

because $18$ of the $27$ points have $x = \pm 1$, and likewise for $y$. So $T_z = \frac{3 \cdot 17496}{4 \cdot 6} = 2187$ and $T = 3 \cdot 2187 = 6561$. The remainder is $561$.
